workItems.title: Product roadmap and machine-readable handoff state
acceptance: Roadmap states vision, boundaries, principles, workstreams, milestones and handoff protocol
Machine-readable state records status, dependencies, acceptance criteria and last-session handoff
A zero-dependency command rejects inconsistent state
workItems.notes: This state tracks Buaflow product development, not an adopter project's lifecycle state.

workItems.title: Readiness levels and Deployment-Ready Contract
acceptance: R0 through R4 have non-overlapping outcomes and promotion rules
R3 defines portable deployment without source-code changes
Conditional controls require an explicit not-applicable rationale

workItems.title: Readiness manifest validator v1
acceptance: A versioned manifest template represents target level, commit, controls and evidence
A zero-dependency validator fails missing, failed or unsupported controls
File evidence paths are checked and JSON output is available for CI
Automated tests cover pass, fail and not-applicable behavior
workItems.notes: V1 validates evidence declarations; BF-005/EP work will make production execution fail-closed and generate immutable evidence.

workItems.title: Core regression tests for scripts, hooks and gates
acceptance: Critical script branches have automated tests on Windows and Linux-compatible Node APIs
Gate skip/warn/fail behavior is covered
A single repository command runs syntax and regression checks
workItems.notes: The first regression run exposed and fixed positional root parsing in docs-lint.js.

workItems.title: Fail-closed production mode
acceptance: Production mode fails when verify or a required scanner is unavailable
R3 claims cannot pass with skipped mandatory checks
Adoption mode remains backward compatible and reports degraded assurance
workItems.notes: Production assurance is opt-in and fail-closed; adoption remains the backward-compatible default.

workItems.title: Canonical artifact schemas and migration policy
acceptance: Public machine-readable artifacts have schema IDs and versions
Backward compatibility and migration rules are documented and tested
workItems.notes: Public v1 contracts cover stack config, readiness manifest, prototype flow and pixel config; vendor-owned JSON is explicitly excluded.

workItems.title: Vendor-neutral CLI shell
acceptance: CLI exposes init, doctor, verify, readiness and resume without requiring an AI vendor
Every command has stable exit codes and machine-readable output
workItems.notes: The CLI shell owns stable exit codes and JSON envelopes; it delegates stack-specific controls instead of reimplementing them.

workItems.title: Product graph schema v1
acceptance: Schema captures actors, outcomes, capabilities, rules, entities, integrations, NFRs, assumptions, risks and exclusions
A human-readable view can be generated without losing canonical data
workItems.notes: v1 covers the 10 required categories with cross-references by id; claude-setup/product-graph.js renders a Markdown view and self-verifies every leaf value from the source JSON appears in it before printing. Not yet wired into the intent/spec/plan/task chain (IC-002/IC-003) or profile selection (PP-001).

workItems.title: Application profile contract v1
acceptance: Profiles alter required controls, architecture choices and clarification questions
At least content, internal CRUD and SaaS profiles have fixtures
workItems.notes: Each control override cross-checks against claude-setup/readiness.js's own control catalog and conditional set, so not-applicable is only ever legal where the readiness contract already allows it. Schema requires at least one control override, architecture choice and clarification question per profile, so a profile that changes nothing cannot validate. content/internal-crud/saas fixtures are proven to genuinely disagree (persistence, database-migration, accessibility) by an automated test, not just asserted. Not yet wired into buaflow init/doctor or the CLI — that is PP-002/CLI follow-up work.

workItems.title: Stack and capability pack contracts
acceptance: Pack contract defines inputs, generated artifacts, compatibility, verification, upgrade and operational evidence
Pack validation is deterministic
workItems.notes: One shared v1 contract covers both stack and capability packs via a kind discriminator, matching this item's merged scope (the long-term roadmap's PP-002/PP-006 split is deferred). operationalEvidence[].control cross-checks against claude-setup/readiness.js's control catalog, the same mechanism PP-001 uses, so a pack must name a real control it helps satisfy. generatedArtifacts/verification/operationalEvidence all require minItems 1, so a pack that generates nothing or proves nothing cannot validate. nextjs-postgres (stack) and auth-rbac (capability, requiresPacks nextjs-postgres) fixtures prove the contract works for both kinds and contribute evidence to different controls. No generator executes yet — that is PP-003 (building the actual reference app).

workItems.title: First web golden stack and R3 reference app
acceptance: Reference app reaches R3 from a clean environment without source changes
All evidence and elapsed time are retained as an eval fixture
workItems.notes: 25/25 R3 controls pass with real, checked evidence (see evidence/pp-003-eval-fixture.json): tests, Docker build, migration/rollback rehearsal, clean-environment rehearsal, SBOM, dependency/secrets scans, accessibility/performance checks, and a real green GitHub Actions run (https://github.com/Khattiya01/buaflow/actions/runs/35758419510) after committing and pushing with explicit user consent. The local clean-environment rehearsal (docker-only) did not catch three gaps that the first real CI run did: a typecheck script depending on stale Next.js typegen output, an --env-file that hard-fails with no .env present, and a dependency-audit step that would have red-lined forever on a documented, understood finding (prisma CLI's peer-dependency chain, proven absent from the shipped image). All three fixed and re-verified before the run that finally passed. Correction during PP-004 (2026-09-23): this verification command was missing --root, so it failed if run exactly as originally written (file evidence resolves relative to --root, which defaults to cwd, not to the manifest's own directory) — fixed here without changing PP-003's actual pass/fail outcome, which was independently re-confirmed.

workItems.title: Second web golden stack and R3 reference app
acceptance: A second, materially different web stack (e.g. React + FastAPI + PostgreSQL, per BUAFLOW_PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md) reaches R3 from a clean environment, proving the pack contract generalizes beyond nextjs-postgres
All evidence and elapsed time are retained as an eval fixture, comparable to PP-003's
workItems.notes: 25/25 R3 controls pass with real, checked evidence (see evidence/pp-004-eval-fixture.json): 22 backend tests (pytest, real Postgres), 6 Playwright e2e tests (primary flow, accessibility, performance), strict mypy + ruff clean, real Docker build, a real Alembic upgrade/downgrade/upgrade rehearsal (a genuine native rollback, unlike PP-003's hand-written rollback.sql companion for forward-only Prisma), a real clean-environment rehearsal, SBOMs and dependency/secrets scans for both the Python backend and the npm frontend, and a real green GitHub Actions run (https://github.com/Khattiya01/buaflow/actions/runs/35765907597) after committing and pushing with the user's prior go-ahead to continue autonomously — reached on the FIRST push, no fix-iterate rounds needed (unlike PP-003's three). One real finding along the way, caught locally before pushing: pip-audit found 7 known advisories in starlette 0.46.2 (pulled in transitively by fastapi's loose >=0.46.0 bound); fixed by pinning starlette directly to >=1.6,<1.7, not documented-and-ignored — see docs/security-notes.md. Also caught and fixed a real, unrelated gap: PP-003's own recorded readiness verification command (this same PP-004 entry's sibling, above) was missing --root and would not have actually reproduced a pass as originally written — corrected there without changing PP-003's already-recorded outcome. No capability-pack equivalent of auth-rbac exists yet for this stack (v1's pack contract has no capability-based requiresPacks, same PP-007 gap) — auth/RBAC is built directly into the app; flagged as a follow-up, not attempted here.

workItems.title: Core capability packs
acceptance: Core capability packs cover database persistence, object storage, notifications, background jobs and audit logging, alongside the existing auth-rbac pack
A composed set of packs is checked deterministically for missing dependencies, declared conflicts and generated-file collisions
workItems.notes: 5 new capability packs (db, storage, notification, background-jobs, audit-log) alongside PP-002's existing nextjs-postgres/auth-rbac — matches the roadmap's 'auth, RBAC/ownership, DB, storage, notification, background jobs, audit log' list (auth+RBAC/ownership covered by the existing auth-rbac pack). claude-setup/pack-composition.js is new: it checks whether a chosen SET of packs installs together cleanly — missing requiresPacks, both sides of a conflictsWithPacks pair present, or two packs writing the same generatedArtifacts path undeclared. Building it immediately surfaced a real v1 contract gap: requiresPacks is identity-based ('needs pack X'), not capability-based ('needs something providing persistence'), so background-jobs/audit-log can't machine-declare their real dependency on db-or-nextjs-postgres — documented in templates/pack.tpl.json and each fixture's description rather than papered over. Also added db to nextjs-postgres's conflictsWithPacks (and vice versa), since nextjs-postgres already bundles persistence. A small step toward M2's 'convergence checks', not the whole of it.

workItems.title: Evidence bundle format
acceptance: A single evidence bundle format wraps a readiness.json manifest, a human-readable report index and immutable run metadata (commit, timestamps, tool versions), per the roadmap's one-line description

The format is stack-agnostic: PP-003 (nextjs-postgres-crud) and PP-004 (react-fastapi-postgres-crud) can both produce a valid bundle from their existing evidence/ directories without app-specific special-casing
workItems.notes: Scope confirmed with the user before starting (D-004): schema + generator script, not schema-only and not provenance/checksums (that stays with EP-004). claude-setup/evidence-bundle.js reuses claude-setup/readiness.js's own validateManifest for the pass/fail summary instead of re-implementing control evaluation, records commit/targetLevel from the readiness manifest it wraps (not from git directly, so it works without a git binary present), and records its OWN generatedAt/toolVersions (node version, platform, arch) at bundle-build time, distinct from the manifest's own generatedAt. Deliberately generic: no stack-specific tool-version detection, so it doesn't special-case any pack. The generated Markdown report index self-checks that every control id/status/evidence/rationale value from the wrapped readiness manifest appears in the rendered document (same technique as claude-setup/product-graph.js), so the 'human-readable' half of the format can't silently drop evidence. A bundle can wrap a FAILING readiness manifest too (summary.ok: false) — the bundle format packages whatever readiness state exists; it does not re-adjudicate R3 pass/fail itself. Registered as a full public artifact type (schema + template + registry entry + v0/v1 migration fixtures), following standards/artifact-versioning.md's own 'adding a new artifact' recipe, not a shortcut. Proven stack-agnostic by actually generating real bundles for both PP-003 and PP-004 from their existing evidence/ directories with zero app-specific code (both R3 PASS 25/25).

workItems.title: Contract mismatch detector: profile vs. composed packs (narrow slice)
acceptance: Given an application profile and a chosen set of packs, a deterministic check flags when the profile marks a control 'not-applicable' but a chosen pack declares operationalEvidence for that exact control (the pack proves the capability exists, contradicting the profile's own rationale)
The check is exercised against the real fixtures (content profile vs. auth-rbac pack) and proven silent on a non-contradicting set
workItems.notes: This is a deliberately narrow slice of the roadmap's full BC-005 ('Contract mismatch detectors: schema/API/migration/UI/requirement drift checks'), pulled forward to close M2's 'convergence checks' completion criterion (D-004) without waiting on BC-001..004 (agent I/O contract, work isolation, scheduler, convergence graph), none of which exist yet. It reuses claude-setup/pack-composition.js (PP-007) and claude-setup/application-profile.js (PP-001) as-is via a new --profile flag and validateProfileFit() export — no new artifact type, no new machinery. Schema/API/migration/UI drift detection (the rest of BC-005's real scope) stays out of scope until BC-001..004 land; do not treat this entry as satisfying the full BC-005 vision from the long-term roadmap table.

workItems.title: Mobile golden stack
acceptance: A mobile reference app (Expo or Flutter, per BUAFLOW_PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md) reaches R3 from a clean environment, including a documented sync/offline contract
All evidence and elapsed time are retained as an eval fixture, comparable to PP-003/PP-004's, and the app produces a valid evidence bundle (EP-001) without app-specific special-casing
workItems.notes: Not started. current.focus moved here only because M2's own completion criteria (two web stacks, core capability packs, convergence checks, evidence bundle) are now all done and current.focus cannot be empty — this is the roadmap's own next-listed item and lastSession.next had already flagged it as a candidate. Stack choice (Expo vs. Flutter) and scope are real design decisions and should be confirmed with the user before starting, the same pattern EP-001 and PP-004 followed.

workItems.title: Canonical workflow protocol (rules, skills, agents)
acceptance: core/rules/*.md defines a vendor-neutral workflow rule contract (description + triggerPaths + body markdown) with no Claude-Code-specific syntax

core/skills/*.md and core/agents/*.md define vendor-neutral contracts for skills and subagents, abstracting the concepts that generalize across vendors ({{ARGUMENTS}}, {{shell: ...}}, invocation: human|human-or-model, modelTier: fast|balanced|deep) while leaving Claude Code's own tool-permission DSL (claudeAllowedTools, claudeTools) as an explicit, honestly-labeled passthrough rather than a guessed-at neutral shape
All 6 existing workflow rules, all 10 existing skills and all 3 existing subagents are represented in core/ without content loss
Hooks and settings.json remain explicitly out of scope and documented as follow-up in core/README.md, not silently dropped
workItems.notes: Pulled forward from its nominal M4 milestone ahead of M3/PP-005 at the user's explicit request (see D-006) — Claude Code adapter only, Codex/Copilot deferred. Started as a deliberately narrow rules-only slice in an earlier part of this same session (proving the core→generator pattern on content with zero Claude-Code-specific syntax), then extended to skills and agents in the same session at the user's request (see D-007) once the pattern was proven. Skills/agents required real design work rules didn't: which Claude-Code-specific mechanics generalize across vendors ($ARGUMENTS → {{ARGUMENTS}}, inline `` !`bash` `` execution → {{shell: ...}}, disable-model-invocation → invocation: human, model: haiku/sonnet/opus → modelTier: fast/balanced/deep — all genuinely portable concepts) versus which don't (allowed-tools permission DSL like `Bash(git *)`, and the subagent tools: list) — the latter are kept as explicit `claudeAllowedTools`/`claudeTools` passthrough fields, honestly labeled as not-yet-neutral, rather than inventing an unproven taxonomy with only one real consumer to validate it against (see core/README.md's mapping table for the full reasoning per field). Hooks (`claude-setup/hooks/*.js`) and `settings.json.tpl` remain out of scope — they are executable code and Claude Code's own permission/event-binding format, not prompt/instruction content, and need their own neutral-shape question answered first. Proven lossless, not just asserted: regenerating all of claude-setup/rules, claude-setup/skills and claude-setup/agents from this core reproduced the previously hand-authored files byte-for-byte (empty git diff) for all 19 files (6 rules + 10 skills + 3 agents). Investigated extending to hooks/settings.json.tpl later in this same session, at the user's request, and concluded NOT to (see D-008): unlike rules/skills/agents, hooks have no content/wrapper split to exploit — the JS *is* the vendor-specific implementation, wired directly to Claude Code's own stdin JSON tool_input schema, hookSpecificOutput stdout format, exit-code-2-means-block convention and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR env var, with match logic that is not uniformly declarative (e.g. guard-bash.js's main-branch rule shells out to `git rev-parse` rather than matching the command string alone). Forcing a core/hooks/ would mean either copying the same JS unchanged (no actual abstraction) or inventing a guard-rule DSL with no second adapter to validate the design against — the same trap already avoided for claudeAllowedTools/claudeTools, at larger scale. This is a considered, investigated conclusion, not an unexamined gap — do not silently retry it without new information (e.g. a real second adapter to design against).

workItems.title: Claude Code adapter (rules, skills, agents)
acceptance: claude-setup/rules/*.md, claude-setup/skills/*/SKILL.md and claude-setup/agents/*.md are generated from core/ by scripts/generate-workflow-{rules,skills,agents}.js, not hand-maintained
npm run check fails if any of the three generated sets drifts from their core/ source, so they cannot silently diverge
A README documents the adapter pattern (core → per-vendor generator) so a future Codex/Copilot adapter is understood as a new generator against the same core, not a new content fork
workItems.notes: Wired into npm run check (scripts/check-repository.js) as three steps — 'workflow rules/skills/agents (core → Claude adapter)' — same pattern as the roadmap/artifact/test steps already there. claude-setup/agents/README.md (documentation, not an agent definition) is explicitly excluded from the drift check since it has no core/agents/ source. MT-003 (Codex adapter) and MT-004 (Copilot/Kiro adapters) are explicitly NOT attempted here per the user's direction (2026-09-23) and the standing vendor-scope preference (keep new contracts vendor-neutral only when free; don't build other vendor adapters unasked) — do not start them without being asked again. Hooks (`claude-setup/hooks/*.js`) and `claude-setup/settings.json.tpl` remain hand-maintained Claude-only content, not yet core-derived — see MT-001's notes for why.

workItems.title: Evidence and pain-point discovery layer before intent
acceptance: Evidence register template captures source, owner, date, coverage and a confidence level (measured, observed, reported or assumed)

A single process-flow template covers both as-is and to-be process mapping (actor, trigger, action, system, output, wait time, handoff and a pain-point id per step for as-is; change id, pain resolved, what becomes automated, what stays human judgment and a success metric for to-be)
Pain-point register template captures workflow/step, symptom, evidence id, frequency, impact, workaround, root cause, confidence and priority
standards/discovery-and-validation.md defines when this layer is required versus optional, so small tasks are never forced through it
Phase 1 and Phase A reference the new templates as an opt-in step before requirement gathering, gated on new-product or major-initiative scale work, not every /intent
workItems.notes: Adopted from an external research review on 2026-09-23 (see D-005). Deliberately opt-in, not a mandatory gate, to keep the existing Progressive rigor principle intact — this must not become required ceremony for small tasks. Gating criteria in standards/discovery-and-validation.md is a 3-condition table (new-product, major-initiative touching multiple workflows/roles across >1 milestone, or the problem is still opinion-only with no evidence) with an explicit 'default is skip' statement, so it composes with (not on top of) /intent's own existing track:trivial check rather than adding a second gate everyone has to clear. phases/07-handoff.md's Phase 7 install map was also updated (not in the original artifacts list) to actually copy the 3 new templates into adopter projects and create docs/discovery/ — without this, the templates would exist in buaflow/ but never reach an adopter, silently breaking the 'opt-in step' claim. No JSON schema/registry entry was added for these templates (unlike state/readiness/pack etc.) since nothing currently needs to parse them automatically — plain markdown matches every other discovery-layer template in this repo (intent/spec/plan/task/adr); revisit only if DV-002's traceability check needs real parsing.

workItems.title: Traceability chain extended upstream to evidence and pain points
acceptance: docs-lint can check that an intent references a pain-point id when the discovery layer (DV-001) was used for that project
Missing linkage produces a warning, not a hard failure, so projects that skip the discovery layer are unaffected
Existing intent/spec/plan/task trace checks in docs-lint keep passing unchanged
workItems.notes: Adopted from an external research review on 2026-09-23 (see D-005). Scoped to pain-point ids only, not the acceptance text's 'or objective id' — no 'objective' artifact type exists anywhere in this system yet (checked schemas/, templates/, IC-001's product-graph 'outcomes' category is a different, unwired concept), so checking for one would mean inventing an undefined concept; deliberately left out rather than guessed at, same posture as other narrow-slice decisions this session (D-006/D-007/D-008). Also scoped to intents only, not 'a feature' (spec) — specs already trace back to their source intent via docs-lint's existing check #7 (accepted intent must be pointed to by a task or spec), so checking intents alone extends the traceability chain upstream through that existing link without duplicating the check at the spec layer. The gate condition is the coarsest possible: any project without docs/discovery/pain-point-register.md is completely unaffected (the whole new check block is skipped), matching the acceptance text's 'projects that skip the discovery layer are unaffected' literally, not just approximately. Caught and fixed one real bug found while building this: the pain-point-register template's own example row used PP-001 (a real-looking id) instead of the -000 sentinel convention this repo already uses for template placeholders (T-000, I-000) — copying the template verbatim would have produced a false 'real' pain point immediately; fixed to PP-000 in the template (and EVD-000 in evidence-register.tpl.md, CH-000 in process-flow.tpl.md, for the same reason) before docs-lint.js was written to treat PP-000 specifically as non-real. Also renamed evidence ids from EV-xxx to EVD-xxx (evidence-register.tpl.md, pain-point-register.tpl.md) after noticing EV-xxx already means eval case (docs/evals/EV-000-*.md) in the same adopter docs/ tree — caught before any adopter could hit the collision. 5 new docs-lint tests; full suite 142/142.

workItems.title: Business outcome review after release, distinct from the config-learning loop
acceptance: Outcome-review template records baseline, target, actual metric and a keep/iterate/rollback/monitor/open-new-intent decision

phases/08-tune-and-evolve.md documents outcome review as a separate activity from the existing AGENTS.md/rule/hook config-learning loop, with its own trigger (milestone close or post-release), so the two loops are not conflated
workItems.notes: Adopted from an external research review on 2026-09-23 (see D-005). New §8.9 in phases/08-tune-and-evolve.md opens with an explicit contrast against §8.1 (config-learning loop) — different question (did the AI/process behave correctly vs. did the business pain point actually get fixed), different evidence (AI behavior vs. real business/user metrics), and states plainly that passing §8.1 does not imply §8.9 would pass, so the two cannot be conflated by a reader skimming just one of them. Added a trigger row to the phase's own 'ทำเมื่อไหร่' table (same table DV-002/other triggers already live in) rather than inventing a separate mechanism. The template deliberately reuses the SAME metric named in process-flow.tpl.md's to-be 'success metric' column (not a newly-invented one at review time) — changing what's measured after the fact would let a failing initiative redefine success post-hoc; a metric change is treated as a lesson about the original to-be estimate, not a fresh start. gated the same opt-in way as DV-001/DV-002: only for initiatives that actually have discovery-layer artifacts (docs/discovery/) to review against; ordinary features skip it. phases/07-handoff.md's install map was updated (not in the original artifacts list, same gap-closing reasoning as DV-001) so outcome-review.tpl.md actually reaches adopter projects instead of sitting unused in buaflow/. This closes out all of DV-001..003 (Discovery and Validation workstream) in one session.

decisions.decision: Evolve Buaflow as a model-agnostic application production system, not merge the reviewed AI-DLC starter.
decisions.reason: Buaflow's advantage is enforceable production qualification and portable handoff; the reviewed starter contributes patterns, not a compatible product core.
decisions.impact: Adopt decision records, adapters, traceability and teaching examples selectively while retaining Buaflow's lifecycle and gates.

decisions.decision: Target R3 Production Candidate rather than hosting or deploying applications for users.
decisions.reason: This preserves portability and keeps Buaflow focused on turning intent into verifiable deployable artifacts.
decisions.impact: Deployment rehearsal and manifests are in scope; operating a hosted control plane is not currently in scope.

decisions.decision: Use machine-readable state as canonical and Markdown as the explanatory view.
decisions.reason: Markdown-only completion states drift and cannot reliably drive gates or cross-model handoff.
decisions.impact: New core artifacts require schemas, validators and migration rules.

decisions.decision: Close M2 by (1) scoping EP-001 as a schema + generator script (not schema-only, not provenance/checksums) and (2) satisfying M2's 'convergence checks' criterion with a narrow profile-vs-pack contradiction check inside PP-007's pack-composition.js, tracked as a scoped-down BC-005, instead of waiting on BC-001..004.
decisions.reason: The user asked to jointly decide M2 scope before continuing (2026-09-23). For EP-001, a generator was chosen over a bare schema because a format nobody can produce isn't 'ครบ' (complete) in practice; provenance/checksums were excluded because that is EP-004's named scope and duplicating it there would blur the two. For convergence checks, full BC-005 (schema/API/migration/UI/requirement drift) needs BC-001..004 (agent I/O contract, work isolation, scheduler, convergence graph) which don't exist yet and would be a large, premature ecosystem surface to build just to close M2; PP-007 already noted its pack-composition.js as 'a small step toward M2's convergence checks, not the whole of it', so extending that same tool to catch one real, concrete contradiction (a profile declaring a control not-applicable while a chosen pack proves that exact control) was the smallest true instance of a 'convergence check' available without new machinery.
decisions.impact: M2 ('Repeatable Web Production': two web stacks, core capability packs, convergence checks, evidence bundle) is now fully done. The full BC-005 vision (schema/API/migration/UI/requirement drift detection across BC-001..004) remains open and unscoped; do not treat this BC-005 entry as having satisfied it. current.milestone moves to M3.

decisions.decision: Reviewed an external research document, 'Buaflow: AI-Native SDLC + Agentic Engineering,' written by the user's friend. Added a new 'Discovery and Validation' workstream (DV-001..003) to BUAFLOW_PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md, positioned before Intent Compiler, and pulled DV-001..003 into state.json as backlog. Did not create a separate workstream for the research's proposed Agentic Engineering layer (Orchestrator, Agent Contract, autonomy tiers A0-A4, agent run records) because it substantially overlaps with the already-planned BC-001..007 workstream at M3; added a pointer note after the BC-* table instead so that detail is not lost.
decisions.reason: Comparing the research against the current roadmap and phase docs found two gaps nothing existing covers: no evidence/pain-point/as-is/to-be discovery layer upstream of the Intent Compiler (Phase 1 is requirement Q&A, Phase A is technical inventory only, neither captures pain-point evidence or root cause), and Phase 8's feedback loop is config-learning only, not post-release business-outcome measurement. Everything else the research proposed (Orchestrator, Agent Contract, execution isolation, independent verification) already has a home in BC-001..007. Scoped DV-001..003 as opt-in (not a mandatory gate for every /intent) to keep the existing Progressive rigor principle intact, since the research's proposed process is heavier than small tasks warrant.
decisions.impact: DV-001..003 are backlog, not in current.focus, and do not block or change PP-005/M3 work. They depend only on BF-001 (already done) so they can be picked up independently and in order (DV-001 first; DV-002/DV-003 depend on DV-001 or are independent of it) whenever the user chooses. BC-001..007's future scoping at M3 should reference the research's autonomy-tier and agent-contract detail per the new note in the roadmap.

decisions.decision: Pulled MT-001 (canonical workflow protocol) and MT-002 (Claude Code adapter) forward from their nominal M4 milestone into active work, ahead of finishing M3/PP-005, and completed both within this session as a deliberately narrow first slice covering workflow rules only (claude-setup/rules/*.md). MT-003 (Codex adapter) and MT-004 (Copilot/Kiro adapters) were explicitly not started.
decisions.reason: The user asked to continue working but redirected scope: build only the Claude Code adapter, leave Codex/Copilot for later, and skip PP-005 (mobile) for now. Confirmed with the user before starting (this session, 2026-09-23) that (1) this is a deliberate reorder ahead of M3, not an accidental milestone skip, and (2) the adapter should be a real vendor-neutral core + generator split proven with one real consumer (Claude Code), not just documentation of the existing claude-setup/ content. Scoped to rules only because claude-setup/rules/*.md was already pure frontmatter (`paths:`) + markdown body with zero Claude-Code-specific syntax — it round-trips through a neutral core losslessly. Skills and agents embed real Claude-Code-specific mechanics (`$ARGUMENTS`, inline `` !`bash` `` execution, `allowed-tools` permission strings, `disable-model-invocation`, subagent `model:` hints) that need their own neutral representation designed deliberately; attempting that in the same pass risked a rushed, wrong design, so it was left as documented follow-up instead (see core/README.md and MT-001's notes).
decisions.impact: current.milestone and current.focus are unchanged by this pull-forward (still M3 / PP-005) — MT-001/MT-002 are simply done now, out of their nominal sequence, the same way BC-005/EP-001 were pulled into M2 ahead of their long-term table position. claude-setup/rules/*.md is now generated output (scripts/generate-workflow-rules.js), checked by npm run check, and must not be hand-edited again. MT-003/MT-004 remain untouched; do not start a Codex or Copilot adapter without the user asking again, per the standing vendor-neutral-scope preference. Canonicalizing skills/agents/hooks/settings into core/ remains open, unscoped future work — not committed to any milestone.

decisions.decision: Extended MT-001/MT-002 (in the same session as D-006) from rules-only to also cover skills and subagents: core/skills/*.md and core/agents/*.md now exist alongside core/rules/*.md, generated into claude-setup/skills/*/SKILL.md and claude-setup/agents/*.md by two new generators. Designed neutral representations for the Claude-Code-specific mechanics that generalize across vendors ({{ARGUMENTS}}, {{shell: ...}}, invocation: human|human-or-model, modelTier: fast|balanced|deep), while deliberately NOT inventing a neutral shape for the ones that don't have a second vendor to validate against (allowed-tools permission DSL, subagent tools: list) — those stay as explicit claudeAllowedTools/claudeTools passthrough fields.
decisions.reason: The user asked to continue after MT-001/MT-002's rules-only commit, and picked 'extend the adapter to skills/agents' over the other two open threads (PP-005, DV-001) when asked. Rules alone proved the core→generator pattern but left the harder half of MT-001's scope (skills/agents, which is where the real Claude-Code-specific syntax lives) undone. Before writing any core content, inventoried every skill/agent's frontmatter and body for Claude-Code-specific mechanics ($ARGUMENTS, inline `` !`bash` `` execution, allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation, subagent model:/tools:) across all 10 skills and 3 agents, then made a deliberate call per mechanic: abstract it when the underlying concept is genuinely cross-vendor (argument passthrough, inline-command execution, human-only invocation, and model cost/capability tiers all have clear equivalents in other agentic CLIs), but leave it as an honestly-labeled vendor passthrough when it's Claude Code's own DSL with no second implementation to prove a neutral shape against (the allowed-tools Bash(pattern) syntax, and even the simpler agent tools: list, for consistency with that same reasoning) — avoiding the trap of inventing a 'neutral' schema for something unproven, per the roadmap's own 'don't build ecosystem surface before contracts stabilize' principle.
decisions.impact: MT-001/MT-002's acceptance/artifacts/notes were rewritten in place (not duplicated as new MT-00x entries) since they represent the same ongoing 'canonical protocol + Claude adapter' effort — their titles dropped '(narrow slice: rules)' since that slice is now subsumed. All 19 core-sourced files (6 rules + 10 skills + 3 agents) are proven byte-identical to their previously hand-authored claude-setup/ counterparts via git diff, the same rigor as the rules-only pass. npm run check now runs three drift checks (rules/skills/agents). Still explicitly out of scope: hooks (claude-setup/hooks/*.js, executable code) and settings.json.tpl (Claude Code's own permission/event-binding format) — neither is prompt/instruction content like rules/skills/agents, and each needs its own neutral-shape question answered before being pulled into core/. MT-003/MT-004 (Codex/Copilot adapters) remain untouched per the standing vendor-scope preference.

decisions.decision: Investigated extending MT-001/MT-002's core/ to hooks (claude-setup/hooks/*.js) and settings.json.tpl, at the user's request immediately after D-007, and concluded NOT to build it — no code was written for this scope. Recorded the conclusion in MT-001's notes so it is not silently re-investigated later without new information.
decisions.reason: Read all 5 hook scripts and settings.json.tpl before deciding. Unlike rules/skills/agents, hooks have no content/wrapper split to exploit: each hook script IS the vendor-specific implementation, not prose content wrapped in vendor syntax. Every hook reads Claude Code's own stdin JSON tool_input schema (tool_input.command / file_path / content / new_string / edits[].new_string, all Claude Code's exact tool-call shapes), writes Claude Code's own hookSpecificOutput stdout protocol, uses Claude Code's exit-code-2-means-block convention, and reads the CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR env var. The guard logic itself is not uniformly declarative either — e.g. guard-bash.js's 'block merge into main' rule shells out to `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` and checks the live branch, not just a regex on the command text; guard-new-component.js parses a markdown table as a registry. settings.json.tpl's permissions.allow/deny is Claude Code's own Bash(pattern) permission-string syntax and its hooks: block is Claude Code's own event-matcher format. Forcing a core/hooks/ would mean either copying the identical JS into core/ unchanged (zero actual abstraction, dishonest to call vendor-neutral) or inventing a guard-rule DSL (match predicates + a translation layer to Claude's I/O contract) with no second adapter to validate the design against — the exact trap already avoided for claudeAllowedTools/claudeTools in D-007, but larger and riskier here since there's no proven-safe subset to abstract first.
decisions.impact: core/ stays at 3 sub-layers (rules, skills, agents) — no core/hooks/ or core/settings/ this session. claude-setup/hooks/*.js and settings.json.tpl remain 100% hand-maintained Claude-only content, unchanged by this session. This is a considered, investigated conclusion, not an unexamined gap — a future session should not retry the same approach without a genuine reason to revisit (e.g. a real second adapter under construction that needs the guard-rule policy expressed neutrally, which would finally give the design something real to validate against). MT-003/MT-004 (Codex/Copilot adapters) remain untouched. No open thread was created by this decision; PP-005 and DV-001..003 are the only remaining open threads from before.

lastSession.summary: After D-008 closed the hooks/settings.json investigation (no code, decision only, already committed), the user asked to keep working autonomously through the rest of the plan and signed off for the night. With PP-005 still explicitly skipped, the only dependency-satisfied backlog left was DV-001..003 (Discovery and Validation), so all three were built and closed out in sequence in this session: DV-001 added the 3 opt-in templates (evidence-register, process-flow, pain-point-register) and standards/discovery-and-validation.md with an explicit 3-condition gating table (default is skip), referenced from Phase 1 and Phase A, and wired into Phase 7's install map (phases/07-handoff.md — not in DV-001's original artifact list, added because the templates would otherwise never reach an adopter project). DV-002 added a warn-only docs-lint check (claude-setup/docs-lint.js) that flags intents with no pain-point linkage, but ONLY when a project's own pain-point register has real (non-template) rows — projects that never used discovery are completely unaffected, not just lightly touched; scoped to pain-point ids only ('objective id' was left out since no such artifact type exists anywhere in this system, rather than guessing at one), and to intents only (specs already inherit traceability transitively via docs-lint's existing intent→spec check). DV-003 added templates/outcome-review.tpl.md and a new §8.9 in phases/08-tune-and-evolve.md that opens by explicitly contrasting itself with §8.1's config-learning loop so the two are never conflated, and deliberately reuses the same success metric already committed to in process-flow.tpl.md's to-be column rather than letting reviewers redefine success after the fact. While building DV-001, caught and fixed a real bug before it could ship: the pain-point-register template's own example row used a realistic-looking id (PP-001) instead of this repo's existing '-000 means placeholder' sentinel convention (T-000, I-000) — fixed across all 4 new templates (PP-000/EVD-000/CH-000) before DV-002's docs-lint check was written to rely on that exact convention. Also caught and fixed evidence-register.tpl.md's ids colliding with the pre-existing EV-xxx eval-case id space in the same adopter docs/ tree — renamed to EVD-xxx before any adopter could hit it. 5 new docs-lint tests added; full suite 142/142 passing throughout. This work is NOT yet committed to git.
